scanner_doubts: svd_intro.md:135,139,198,236,248,250,273,274 - all eight `qe-math-011` (proposed) hits are false positives. There is no probability distribution anywhere in this lecture; `{\mathcal N}` is the null space, declared by the lecture itself at 129: "Let ${\mathcal C}$ denote a column space, ${\mathcal N}$ denote a null space, and ${\mathcal R}$ denote a row space." The cause is the `DIST_AFTER` gate in `check_math_011` (tools/qestyle_rules.py:698, tested at 713), which accepts *any* `(` or `[` following the match as evidence of a parameter list - so `{\mathcal N}(X)` and `{\mathcal N}(X^\top )` qualify. `\mathcal C` and `\mathcal R` escape only because the pattern at 706-708 is restricted to `N|U`. Two possible tightenings: require the parenthesised argument to look like a parameter list (contain a comma, a digit, or `\mu` / `\sigma` / `\theta`), or skip the file when its narrative declares the symbol - a `\mathbb{P}`-free, `\sim`-free file using `{\mathcal N}(\cdot)` as an operator is a set-valued map, not a normal distribution

svd_intro.md:750,757 - `qe-math-002` is measured at 0, but 750 writes `X=\sigma_1U_1{V_1}^{T}+\sigma_2 U_2{V_2}^{T}+\ldots+\sigma_{r} U_{r}{V_{r}}^{T}` and 757 writes `${V_k}^{T}=\tilde{\epsilon_k}$` - four `^{T}` transposes, certainly transposes because the same object is `V^\top` at 640, 650 and 773. Two separate gaps in `supT` (tools/qestyle_rules.py:442-445): its base alternation is a bare capital or a `DECORATED` group, so a brace-wrapped base `{V_1}^{T}` matches nothing (the character before `^` is `}`, which is not in the alternation); and its factor lookahead rejects these anyway, because what follows is `+` at 750 and `=` at 757. Adding `\{[A-Za-z](?:_\{[^{}]*\}|_[A-Za-z0-9])?\}` to the base alternation would catch the shape; the lookahead is the deliberate `Y^T` guard and I would leave it alone rather than trade these four for the data-history false positives it exists to prevent
